links.comparator_used: Prompt with diagnostic category constraints removed (open-ended diagnosis, not limited to the seven predefined conditions plus Other Diagnosis)
links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity for emergent chest-pain diagnoses, and false alarms per 500 encounters
links.effect: Baseline prompt with category constraints: sensitivity 79.3%, specificity 45.2%. Removing category constraints: specificity 94.7%, 140 fewer false alarms per 500, sensitivity 8.8%.
links.tradeoff: Constraints produced systematic over-prediction of rare conditions (more false alarms). Removing them cut false alarms but sensitivity fell to 8.8%, so life-threatening diagnoses would be missed.
links.quote: With baseline prompting, GPT-4o systematically over-predicted rare conditions (sensitivity 79.3%; specificity 45.2%); adding prevalence cues or removing diagnostic category constraints respectively increased specificity (83.0% and 94.7%) while reducing false alarms by 107 and 140 per 500, but at the cost of poor sensitivity (30.4% and 8.8%).

links.outcome: Diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and false alarms for life-threatening chest-pain etiologies
links.effect: Baseline prompting: sensitivity 79.3%; specificity 45.2%. Adding prevalence cues: specificity 83.0%; false alarms reduced by 107 per 500; sensitivity 30.4%.
links.tradeoff: Poor sensitivity after adding prevalence cues: 30.4%.
